name: SIGMA - On-Host Password Spray Indicator via Failed Logons With No Real Source (Windows Security 4625) [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/auth_win_bruteforce_onhost_spray.yml (issue #396, filed from a security-auditor review finding on #370's own review: excluding the 4 IpAddress sentinel values from auth-win-bruteforce-source-spray.ndjson correctly stopped local/console/service-account 4625 noise from collapsing into one false severity:high alert, but as a side effect also removed the only coverage that rule accidentally had for a genuine ON-HOST password spray - e.g. runas/LogonUser() API calls from an already-landed foothold, which log 4625 with IpAddress:"-" too, indistinguishable by IP alone from routine local noise). Buckets Security 4625 failed logons WHERE IpAddress IS one of the 4 sentinel values ("-", "0.0.0.0", "::", "") - the exact complement of auth-win-bruteforce-source-spray.ndjson's query - by winlog.computer_name instead of IpAddress (no real network source exists for this population), and alerts when a single host sees >=6 distinct target accounts (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName cardinality) within a 5-minute window. Severity medium, not high like its sibling: an on-host spray from an already-landed foothold is a post-compromise indicator, not the initial-access signal the network-sourced sibling rule represents, so it is scored and triaged differently even though the underlying cardinality logic is identical. "from": "now-10m" / "interval": "5m" is pinned from day one to the #393-corrected lookback >= interval + detection_window formula (its sibling rule's own fix), guaranteeing full containment of a real sliding 5-minute window in one evaluation rather than needing a later retrofit. Verified against the sibling rule as an exact complement: every real 4625 event matches exactly one of the two queries (IpAddress is either sentinel or non-sentinel), never both and never neither, so there is no double-counting or duplicate-alert overlap between them.
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: A misconfigured application or service account retrying the same stale credential against many local resources.
A scheduled task or script iterating stale credentials against several local accounts after a credential rotation.
